data.hypothesis: With the selected parent's 8x16 AVX-512 kernel and KC=128 unchanged, widening only the B-panel column extent from NC=128 to 256 should halve the number of column-panel iterations at n=1024 and reuse each A tile over twice as many output columns. That may reduce synchronization and improve A reuse, while the doubled scratch-panel size may offset those gains. The direct-access cutoff remains 256 to isolate panel width.

memory_lessons.applicability: For this GEMM variant, use matched microkernels and input sizes when judging B packing; prior evidence favored B-packed 8x16 over direct 8x16, while the small measured difference from adding A packing is not conclusive.
memory_lessons.claim: The supplied records report 0.005633 s for direct 8x16, 0.003443 s for B-packed 8x16, and 0.003389 s with an additional A panel; the latest direct 16x16 program measured 0.005219 s. All four catalog programs were distinct and valid, but these observations do not establish that a wider panel will help.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this B-only NC=256 variant against the selected B-only NC=128 parent with the same correctness cases and repeated n=1024 timings.

data.notes: The catalog contains four distinct valid programs and no repeated programs. The closest matched comparison reports 0.005633 s for direct 8x16 versus 0.003443 s for B-packed 8x16; adding an A panel measured 0.003389 s, a small difference that should not be assumed meaningful. The selected parent is the B-only NC=128 program. This candidate changes its B column-panel width while retaining KC, the microkernel, packing layout, thread cap, and direct-path cutoff. No correctness result or timing is available yet for this candidate; the controller must validate it and report repeated native timings. No failed attempt is present in the supplied records.
transformations: Increase the packed B column panel from NC=128 to NC=256 while retaining KC=128 and the existing K-major contiguous-column panel layout.
Keep the 8x16 AVX-512 FMA microkernel, its runtime feature check and scalar fallback, and the 256-element direct-access cutoff unchanged.
Retain disjoint OpenMP output-tile ownership with at most eight threads, generic row/column/K tails, per-call scratch allocation, and full output overwrite on each invocation.
